speaking.prompt: Tell me your name, where you're from, and what you do.
speaking.prompt_tr: Dime tu nombre, de dónde eres y a qué te dedicas.
speaking.goal: Name, place of origin and job, in simple sentences.
examples: My name is Carlos. I'm from Santo Domingo. I'm a baseball coach.

speaking.prompt: What time do you usually arrive at the academy?
speaking.prompt_tr: ¿A qué hora llegas normalmente a la academia?
speaking.goal: A time, ideally in a sentence with usually.
examples: At six thirty in the morning.

speaking.prompt: Explain what you normally do at work in the morning.
speaking.prompt_tr: Explica qué haces normalmente en el trabajo en la mañana.
speaking.goal: Two or more connected activities in a sequence, present simple.
examples: First I have a meeting with the coaches, then I prepare the field, and at eight we start practice with stretching.

speaking.prompt: Hey Coach, what time does practice start tomorrow? And where do we meet?
speaking.prompt_tr: Un jugador pregunta a qué hora empieza la práctica mañana y dónde se reúnen.
speaking.goal: A time and a meeting place, answering both questions.
examples: Practice starts at eight. We meet on field two, by the batting cages.

speaking.prompt: One of your players keeps making the same mistake in practice. What would you tell him, and why?
speaking.prompt_tr: Un jugador comete el mismo error varias veces. ¿Qué le dirías y por qué?
speaking.goal: A specific correction with a reason, tactful tone.
examples: I'd tell him to slow down and focus on one thing, like keeping his glove in front, because if he tries to fix everything at once he gets frustrated.

speaking.prompt: Some coaches want shorter practices and more video sessions. What do you think about that idea? Explain your opinion.
speaking.prompt_tr: Algunos coaches quieren prácticas más cortas y más sesiones de video. ¿Qué opinas? Explica tu opinión.
speaking.goal: A clear opinion with reasons, acknowledging another view, connected discourse.
examples: I think it depends on the player. Video helps older players understand their mechanics, but younger players need more reps on the field, so I'd keep practice long and add short video sessions.

speaking.prompt: Coach, I'm up next. Anything I should do on this ground ball?
speaking.prompt_tr: Antes de una repetición de roletazo, el jugador te pregunta qué debe hacer. Dale una o dos instrucciones.
speaking.goal: One or two short, clear imperative cues (e.g. stay low, glove out front, move your feet, come get it), with 'your' before body parts and equipment. Band A1–A2.
speaking.goal_tr: Una o dos instrucciones cortas y claras (por ejemplo: stay low, glove out front, move your feet), con 'your' delante de las partes del cuerpo.
examples: Stay low and keep your glove out front.
Move your feet and come get it. Glove down early.

speaking.prompt: Coach, what should I focus on during this drill?
speaking.prompt_tr: Un jugador te pregunta en qué debe enfocarse durante el ejercicio. Explícale el enfoque y por qué.
speaking.goal: Name one clear focus for the drill and explain why it helps (so, because, that way), optionally checking understanding or asking him to show it. Band B1–B2.
speaking.goal_tr: Nombra un enfoque claro para el ejercicio y explica por qué ayuda; si puedes, comprueba que te entendió.
examples: Just focus on your first step. If you read it off the bat and get a quick first step, you'll get a better angle and you won't have to rush the throw.
Today I want you to set your feet before every throw, because that's where your accuracy comes from. Show me on the first one.
